subject.title: fix(net): cap default outbound HTTP connection pool limits

question: After repairing constructor-time propagation, should OpenClaw’s public shared proxy factories impose defaults of 256 connections per origin and 1024 total Node sockets?
rationale: The propagation defect is mechanical, but selecting global throughput limits across core and plugin callers requires maintainer intent and representative workload judgment.

options.title: Repair and adopt caps
options.body: Pass the defaults through proxyline’s constructor-owned state and land after representative Node and Undici runtime proof.

options.title: Repair with retuned values
options.body: Keep shared bounds but choose limits from expected provider, plugin, proxy, queueing, and timeout workloads.

options.title: Keep dependency defaults
options.body: Drop global shared limits and apply connection budgets only in workload-specific owners with defined concurrency requirements.

recommendation.title: Repair and adopt caps
recommendation.body: Pass the defaults through proxyline’s constructor-owned state and land after representative Node and Undici runtime proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This login introduced and repeatedly maintained the canonical shared Node and Undici networking paths affected by the policy.
